newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X investor committed suicide in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X investor committed suicide in Canada.

text.p: A Canadian man who committed suicide last month probably was despondent over big losses from an investment in Bre-X Minerals Ltd. stock, police said Friday.

Lawrence Beadle, a 62-year-old lawyer in New Westminster, British Columbia, shot himself to death on April 7. He left no note but family members told police that he had been depressed over his losses in Bre-X.
While Beadle's death was reported as a suicide last month, the connection to losses in Bre-X was not immediately publicised.

Sgt. David Jones of the New Westminster police said investigators had been unable to make a direct link between Bre-X and the suicide because of the absence of a note. But he said they believed that was the most likely reason.
"It was a big contributing factor. He was depressed over what happened to his large investment in Bre-X stock," Jones said.

Bre-X shares collapsed in late March after doubts were raised over its claim to have discovered a huge gold deposit in Indonesia. Independent auditors said on Sunday the claim appeared to be a fraud of almost unprecedented proportions.
The once high-flying stock plunged to just pennies a share when it reopened for trading on Tuesday before being delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange and Nasdaq markets.
Jones said police did not know how many Bre-X shares Beadle had owned. The Vancouver Sun newspaper reported that his losses were around C$3 million ($2.2 million).
The newspaper quoted a police report saying Beadle had been trying to arrange secured loans to cover his losses.
